verses.original: Καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: Kai hoi Pharisaioi kai tines tōn grammateōn elthontes apo Hierosolymōn synagontai pros auton
verses.literal: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around . . . [Jesus]

verses.original: καὶ ἰδόντες ὅτι τινὰς τῶν αὐτοῦ μαθητῶν ἐσθίουσιν τοὺς ἄρτους χερσίν κοιναῖς τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις
verses.transliteration: kai idontes hoti tinas tōn autou mathētōn esthiousin tous artous chersin koinais tout’ estin aniptois
verses.literal: and they saw - some of His disciples eating . . . . . . [with] hands [that were] defiled that is unwashed

verses.original: γὰρ κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων Οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν ἐὰν μὴ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας πυγμῇ
verses.transliteration: gar kratountes tēn paradosin tōn presbyterōn Hoi Pharisaioi kai pantes hoi Ioudaioi ouk esthiousin ean mē nipsōntai tas cheiras pygmē
verses.literal: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders the Pharisees and all the Jews {do} not eat until . . . they wash [their] hands ceremonially

verses.original: καὶ ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν ἐὰν μὴ βαπτίσωνται καὶ ἐστιν πολλά ἄλλα παρέλαβον ἃ κρατεῖν βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων καὶ κλινῶν
verses.transliteration: kai ap’ agoras ouk esthiousin ean mē baptisōntai kai estin polla alla parelabon ha kratein baptismous potēriōn kai xestōn kai chalkiōn kai klinōn
verses.literal: And [on returning] from the market vvv they do not eat unless . . . they wash And there are many other traditions for them - to observe [including] the washing of cups - pitchers - kettles and couches for dining

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν Διὰ τί σου οἱ μαθηταί οὐ περιπατοῦσιν κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἀλλὰ ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον κοιναῖς χερσὶν
verses.transliteration: Kai hoi Pharisaioi kai hoi grammateis eperōtōsin auton Dia ti sou hoi mathētai ou peripatousin kata tēn paradosin tōn presbyterōn alla esthiousin ton arton koinais chersin
verses.literal: So the Pharisees and - scribes questioned [Jesus] Why . . . {do} Your - disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders Instead they eat . . . . . . with defiled hands

verses.original: δὲ Ὁ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἠσαΐας ἐπροφήτευσεν Καλῶς περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν ὡς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τιμᾷ με τοῖς χείλεσίν δὲ αὐτῶν Ἡ καρδία ἀπέχει πόρρω ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ
verses.transliteration: de Ho eipen autois Ēsaias eprophēteusen Kalōs peri hymōn tōn hypokritōn hōs gegraptai hoti Houtos ho laos tima me tois cheilesin de autōn Hē kardia apechei porrō ap’ emou
verses.literal: - - Jesus answered them Isaiah prophesied correctly about you - hypocrites as it is written - These - people honor Me with [their] lips but their - hearts are far from Me

verses.original: δὲ σέβονταί με Μάτην Διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων
verses.transliteration: de sebontai me Matēn Didaskontes didaskalias entalmata anthrōpōn
verses.literal: - They worship Me in vain they teach [as] doctrine [the] precepts of men

verses.original: Ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ κρατεῖτε τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων
verses.transliteration: Aphentes tēn entolēn tou Theou krateite tēn paradosin tōn anthrōpōn
verses.literal: You have disregarded the commandment - of God to keep the tradition - of men

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Καλῶς ἀθετεῖτε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα τηρήσητε ὑμῶν τὴν παράδοσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois Kalōs atheteite tēn entolēn tou Theou hina tērēsēte hymōn tēn paradosin
verses.literal: vvv He went on to say - vvv You neatly set aside the command - of God to maintain your [own] tradition

verses.original: γὰρ Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν Τίμα σου τὸν πατέρα καὶ σου τὴν μητέρα καί Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω
verses.transliteration: gar Mōusēs eipen Tima sou ton patera kai sou tēn mētera kai Ho kakologōn patera ē mētera thanatō teleutatō
verses.literal: For Moses said Honor your - father and your - mother and Anyone who curses [his] father or mother vvv must be put to death

verses.original: δὲ ὑμεῖς λέγετε Ἐὰν ἄνθρωπος εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί Ὃ ἐὰν ὠφεληθῇς ἐξ ἐμοῦ Κορβᾶν ὅ ἐστιν Δῶρον
verses.transliteration: de hymeis legete Ean anthrōpos eipē tō patri ē tē mētri Ho ean ōphelēthēs ex emou Korban ho estin Dōron
verses.literal: But you say that if a man says to [his] father or - mother Whatever . . . you would have received from me [is] Corban (that is a gift devoted [to God] )

verses.original: αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ἀφίετε ποιῆσαι οὐδὲν τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί
verses.transliteration: auton ouketi aphiete poiēsai ouden tō patri ē tē mētri
verses.literal: he [is] no longer permitted to do anything for his father or - mother

verses.original: ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ ὑμῶν παραδόσει ᾗ παρεδώκατε καὶ ποιεῖτε τοιαῦτα πολλὰ παρόμοια
verses.transliteration: akyrountes ton logon tou Theou tē hymōn paradosei hē paredōkate kai poieite toiauta polla paromoia
verses.literal: [Thus] you nullify the word - of God by [the] tradition - you have handed down And you do so in many such [matters]

verses.original: Καὶ πάλιν προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς πάντες Ἀκούσατέ μου καὶ σύνετε
verses.transliteration: Kai palin proskalesamenos ton ochlon elegen autois pantes Akousate mou kai synete
verses.literal: - Once again [Jesus] called the crowd [to Him] [and] said - All of you listen to Me and understand

verses.original: οὐδέν εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐστιν αὐτὸν ἔξωθεν ὃ δύναται κοινῶσαι αὐτόν ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐκπορευόμενά ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: ouden eisporeuomenon eis tou anthrōpou estin auton exōthen ho dynatai koinōsai auton alla ta ekporeuomena ek tou anthrōpou estin ta koinounta ton anthrōpon
verses.literal: Nothing that enters . . . a man - - from the outside - can defile him but the things that come out of a man these are what defile - [him]

verses.original: Καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου εἰς οἶκον αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν τὴν παραβολήν
verses.transliteration: Kai hote eisēlthen apo tou ochlou eis oikon autou hoi mathētai epērōtōn auton tēn parabolēn
verses.literal: - After [Jesus] had left . . . the crowd [and gone] into [the] house His - disciples inquired about . . . the parable

verses.original: ἐστε ὑμεῖς καὶ Οὕτως ἀσύνετοί Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἔξωθεν οὐ δύναται κοινῶσαι αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: este hymeis kai Houtōs asynetoi Kai legei autois ou noeite hoti pan to eisporeuomenon eis ton anthrōpon exōthen ou dynatai koinōsai auton
verses.literal: Are you still so dull - He asked - vvv Do you not understand - Nothing that enters . . . a man from the outside vvv can defile him

verses.original: ὅτι οὐκ εἰσπορεύεται εἰς αὐτοῦ τὴν καρδίαν ἀλλ’ εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν καὶ ἐκπορεύεται εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα πάντα τὰ βρώματα καθαρίζων
verses.transliteration: hoti ouk eisporeuetai eis autou tēn kardian all’ eis tēn koilian kai ekporeuetai eis ton aphedrōna panta ta brōmata katharizōn
verses.literal: because vvv it does not enter . . . his - heart but [it goes] into the stomach and then is eliminated . . . . . . . . . ([Thus] all - foods are clean

verses.original: δὲ Ἔλεγεν ὅτι Τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκεῖνο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: de Elegen hoti To ekporeuomenon ek tou anthrōpou ekeino koinoi ton anthrōpon
verses.literal: - He continued - What comes out of a man that [is what] defiles - [him]

verses.original: γὰρ ἐκ ἔσωθεν τῆς καρδίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐκπορεύονται οἱ κακοὶ οἱ διαλογισμοὶ πορνεῖαι κλοπαί φόνοι μοιχεῖαι
verses.transliteration: gar ek esōthen tēs kardias tōn anthrōpōn ekporeuontai hoi kakoi hoi dialogismoi porneiai klopai phonoi moicheiai
verses.literal: For from within the hearts - of men come - evil - thoughts sexual immorality theft murder adultery

verses.original: πλεονεξίαι πονηρίαι δόλος ἀσέλγεια ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός βλασφημία ὑπερηφανία ἀφροσύνη
verses.transliteration: pleonexiai ponēriai dolos aselgeia ophthalmos ponēros blasphēmia hyperēphania aphrosynē
verses.literal: greed wickedness deceit debauchery envy . . . slander arrogance [and] foolishness

verses.original: πάντα ταῦτα τὰ πονηρὰ ἐκπορεύεται ἔσωθεν καὶ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: panta tauta ta ponēra ekporeuetai esōthen kai koinoi ton anthrōpon
verses.literal: All these - evils come from within and [these are what] defile a man

verses.original: δὲ ἀναστὰς Ἐκεῖθεν ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Τύρου ἤθελεν οὐδένα γνῶναι Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς οἰκίαν καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθη λαθεῖν
verses.transliteration: de anastas Ekeithen apēlthen eis ta horia Tyrou ēthelen oudena gnōnai Kai eiselthōn eis oikian kai ouk ēdynēthē lathein
verses.literal: - [Jesus] left that place [and] went to the region of Tyre Not wanting anyone . . . to know [He was there] - He entered . . . [a] house but vvv was unable to escape their notice

verses.original: ἀλλ’ γυνὴ ἧς τὸ θυγάτριον αὐτῆς εἶχεν ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα εὐθὺς ἀκούσασα περὶ αὐτοῦ ἐλθοῦσα προσέπεσεν πρὸς αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας
verses.transliteration: all’ gynē hēs to thygatrion autēs eichen akatharton pneuma euthys akousasa peri autou elthousa prosepesen pros autou tous podas
verses.literal: Instead a woman whose - little daughter . . . had [an] unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus [and] she came [and] fell at His - feet

verses.original: δὲ ἦν Ἑλληνίς ἡ γυνὴ τῷ Συροφοινίκισσα γένει καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐκβάλῃ τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐκ αὐτῆς τῆς θυγατρὸς
verses.transliteration: de ēn Hellēnis hē gynē tō Syrophoinikissa genei kai ērōta auton hina ekbalē to daimonion ek autēs tēs thygatros
verses.literal: Now she was a Greek - woman of Syrophoenician origin and she kept asking [Jesus] - to drive the demon out of her - daughter

verses.original: πρῶτον Ἄφες τὰ τέκνα χορτασθῆναι Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτῇ γάρ ἐστιν οὐ καλόν λαβεῖν τὸν τῶν τέκνων ἄρτον καὶ βαλεῖν τοῖς κυναρίοις
verses.transliteration: prōton Aphes ta tekna chortasthēnai Kai elegen autē gar estin ou kalon labein ton tōn teknōn arton kai balein tois kynariois
verses.literal: First let the children have their fill - He said . . . For it is not right to take the - children’s bread and toss [it] to the dogs

verses.original: Ναί Κύριε δὲ Ἡ ἀπεκρίθη καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ κυνάρια ὑποκάτω τῆς τραπέζης ἐσθίουσιν ἀπὸ τῶν τῶν παιδίων ψιχίων
verses.transliteration: Nai Kyrie de Hē apekrithē kai legei autō kai ta kynaria hypokatō tēs trapezēs esthiousin apo tōn tōn paidiōn psichiōn
verses.literal: Yes Lord - - she replied . . . . . . . . . even the dogs under the table eat . . . the - children’s crumbs

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Διὰ τοῦτον τὸν λόγον ὕπαγε τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐξελήλυθεν ἐκ σου τῆς θυγατρός
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autē Dia touton ton logon hypage to daimonion exelēlythen ek sou tēs thygatros
verses.literal: Then [Jesus] told her Because of this - answer you may go The demon has left . . . your - daughter

verses.original: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσα εἰς αὐτῆς τὸν οἶκον εὗρεν τὸ παιδίον βεβλημένον ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην καὶ τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐξεληλυθός
verses.transliteration: kai apelthousa eis autēs ton oikon heuren to paidion beblēmenon epi tēn klinēn kai to daimonion exelēlythos
verses.literal: And she went vvv vvv vvv home [and] found [her] child lying on the bed and the demon was gone

verses.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἐξελθὼν ἐκ τῶν ὁρίων Τύρου ἦλθεν διὰ Σιδῶνος εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ὁρίων Δεκαπόλεως
verses.transliteration: Kai palin exelthōn ek tōn horiōn Tyrou ēlthen dia Sidōnos eis tēn thalassan tēs Galilaias ana meson tōn horiōn Dekapoleōs
verses.literal: Then . . . [Jesus] left . . . the region of Tyre [and] went through Sidon to the Sea - of Galilee [and] into . . . the region of [the] Decapolis

verses.original: Καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ κωφὸν καὶ μογιλάλον καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιθῇ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai pherousin autō kōphon kai mogilalon kai parakalousin auton hina epithē tēn cheira autō
verses.literal: - [Some people] brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak and they begged [Jesus] - to place [His] hand on him

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπολαβόμενος αὐτὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ἔβαλεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς δακτύλους εἰς αὐτοῦ τὰ ὦτα καὶ πτύσας ἥψατο αὐτοῦ τῆς γλώσσης
verses.transliteration: Kai apolabomenos auton kat’ idian apo tou ochlou ebalen autou tous daktylous eis autou ta ōta kai ptysas hēpsato autou tēs glōssēs
verses.literal: [So] [Jesus] took him . . . aside privately away from the crowd [and] put His - fingers into [the man’s] - ears Then He spit [and] touched [the man’s] - tongue

verses.original: καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐστέναξεν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἐφφαθά ὅ ἐστιν Διανοίχθητι
verses.transliteration: kai anablepsas eis ton ouranon estenaxen kai legei autō Ephphatha ho estin Dianoichthēti
verses.literal: And looking up to - heaven He sighed deeply and said to him Ephphatha (which means Be opened

verses.original: καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀκοαί ἠνοίγησαν καὶ αὐτοῦ γλώσσης ὁ δεσμὸς τῆς ἐλύθη καὶ ἐλάλει ὀρθῶς
verses.transliteration: kai euthys autou hai akoai ēnoigēsan kai autou glōssēs ho desmos tēs elythē kai elalei orthōs
verses.literal: - Immediately [the man’s] - ears were opened and his tongue vvv vvv vvv was released and he began to speak plainly

verses.original: Καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα λέγωσιν μηδενὶ δὲ ὅσον αὐτοῖς διεστέλλετο αὐτοὶ περισσότερον μᾶλλον ἐκήρυσσον
verses.transliteration: Kai diesteilato autois hina legōsin mēdeni de hoson autois diestelleto autoi perissoteron mallon ekērysson
verses.literal: - [Jesus] ordered them - not to tell anyone . . . But the more He ordered them the more widely . . . they proclaimed [it]

verses.original: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ὑπερπερισσῶς λέγοντες πεποίηκεν πάντα Καλῶς ποιεῖ καὶ τοὺς κωφοὺς ἀκούειν καὶ τοὺς ἀλάλους λαλεῖν
verses.transliteration: kai exeplēssonto hyperperissōs legontes pepoiēken panta Kalōs poiei kai tous kōphous akouein kai tous alalous lalein
verses.literal: - [The people] were utterly astonished . . . [and] said He has done all things well He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak
